blocks.text: Revelation 20 describes the dragon's binding for a thousand years, the reign of those who witnessed to Jesus, the release and final defeat of Satan, and the judgment before the great white throne. Death and Hades give up the dead, the dead are judged according to what is written in the books, and Death and Hades are cast into the lake of fire, called the second death. The chapter names the martyrs' reign the first resurrection without settling every later doctrinal question about the sequence.

sections.title: The thousand years and final judgment

blocks.text: The supplied context says ancient cultures commonly treated death as final, making resurrection a striking claim about God's power and faithfulness. It also notes that Second Temple Judaism debated bodily resurrection. Revelation 20 places that hope within judgment and renewed rule: the dead are raised for judgment, faithful witnesses live and reign, and death itself is finally defeated.

Revelation 20 presents resurrection as part of God's power over death and the renewal of God's people. The chapter's judgment scene does not merely repeat the defeat of a hostile ruler: it includes Death and Hades themselves among what is cast into the lake of fire, making the end of death part of the chapter's final horizon.

sections.title: Death does not have the last word

blocks.text: Revelation 20 describes a thousand-year binding and reign followed by Satan's release, but chronological and symbolic interpretations diverge. The text itself calls the martyrs' life and reign the first resurrection and calls the lake of fire the second death; later systems should be identified as interpretations rather than silently presented as the chapter's only possible reading.
